title: Monte Carlo simulation — probability ranges for wealth and retirement plans
summary: A joke reel with a real explainer in the caption: Monte Carlo simulation runs thousands of randomized market scenarios (crashes, bull runs, inflation, salary and spending changes) to turn a single wealth forecast into a probability band. Instead of "$1M at 65" you get "85% chance of $800K–$1.5M".
takeaways: Model outcomes as distributions, not point forecasts
Stress-test a plan against worst-case paths, not just the median run

title: Carbonyl — full Chromium browser rendered inside your terminal
summary: Carbonyl (github.com/fathyb/carbonyl) is an MIT-licensed Chromium build that renders real web pages directly in a terminal, idling at 0% CPU. Useful for browsing over SSH, headless boxes, or giving terminal-bound agents a real browser.
takeaways: Run a real browser over SSH or on a headless server
MIT-licensed, so you can embed or fork it
Zero idle CPU makes it cheap to leave open in a tmux pane

title: AI-first software design — build data layers agents can actually read
summary: Dashboards and navbars are built for human eyes; agents only see tool-call text, which is why giving Claude raw database access goes wrong. The fix shown: store raw data plus workflow-generated summaries in separate tables and expose tools that return summary-level context first, pulling full transcripts only when needed.
takeaways: Design tool outputs for the agent, not a UI for a human
Store summaries next to raw data so agents fetch the cheap layer first
Return full records only on explicit need to keep context small

title: VidRush — AI tool that builds full YouTube documentaries from a topic
summary: VidRush takes a topic, researches it, writes the script, pulls matching real footage, generates missing visuals with AI, and adds voiceover, music and transitions into a timeline you edit by typing. The reel is a comment-to-get-link promo, so treat the claims as marketing until tested.
takeaways: Topic-to-documentary pipelines now include footage search plus AI fill-ins
Test output quality before building a channel on it

title: Claude Code persistent memory plugin — cross-session recall with fewer tokens
summary: An open-source plugin that gives Claude Code permanent cross-session memory, with a web viewer UI, a bundled skill and a one-command install, claiming up to 95% token savings. The repo name sits in a pinned comment, but the feature list matches claude-mem (thedotmack/claude-mem).
takeaways: Persistent memory plugins cut re-explaining context every session
Verify the 95% token claim on your own workload

title: Ctrl+C vs kill -9 — why SIGINT can be ignored and SIGKILL can't
summary: Ctrl+C sends SIGINT (signal 2) to the whole foreground process group, and programs like vim can catch or ignore it with a signal handler. For a guaranteed stop you escalate to SIGKILL (signal 9) with kill -9 <PID>, which no process can catch, block or ignore.
takeaways: Ctrl+C reaches the whole foreground process group, not one PID
Scripts can trap SIGINT, so it is a request rather than a kill
Use kill -9 only as a last resort; it skips cleanup

title: Claude Code on OpenRouter — keep the harness, swap in cheaper models
summary: When you hit Claude Code's usage limit, you can point it at OpenRouter instead of Anthropic: create an OpenRouter API key and apply a config that reroutes the API base. You keep the agent loop, skills and harness while running whichever model you pick, including free open-weight ones. The exact config is gated behind a comment-for-link.
takeaways: Claude Code's harness can run on non-Anthropic models via OpenRouter
Expect weaker tool-use from small free models
Useful as overflow when you hit plan limits

title: Strait of Hormuz and AIS data — why shadow fleets break the news narrative
summary: Media reports of a closed Strait of Hormuz lean on AIS ship-tracking data, but shadow-fleet vessels go dark or spoof their positions. A research outfit sent an analyst by boat from Oman and found steady traffic, especially Chinese ships on alternate routes. The broader point: single data sources, and AI systems, collapse diversity of thought.
takeaways: AIS is spoofable; treat it as one signal, not truth
Field verification can overturn a consensus built on one dataset
Leaning on one AI or data feed homogenizes conclusions

title: Daniel de Bruin's LEDs in motor oil — light art from used-oil gradients
summary: Light work from Daniel de Bruin (2019): LEDs submerged in used motor oil, which filters the light into a rich color gradient. He built three versions, but the oil degrades everything it touches, so the piece did not last and he has not found a substitute.
takeaways: Dark translucent liquids make natural LED gradient filters
Used oil is corrosive; look for a stable substitute such as tinted mineral oil

title: Turing patterns in Photoshop — repeated blur and sharpen as reaction-diffusion
summary: Blur an image, sharpen it, and repeat many times in Photoshop, and you get leopard-spot and zebra-stripe textures. Blur plays Alan Turing's inhibitor (spreading information) while sharpen plays the activator (boosting local contrast), a digital reaction-diffusion system. Blur and sharpen radii set the scale and type of pattern. Spanish-language reel.
takeaways: Loop blur then sharpen to grow organic patterns from any image
Tune the two radii to control spot size versus stripes
Hide text or shapes in the seed image to get patterned wallpapers
